cli.no_permission: Permission denied on the Kut socket: run this command with sudo (sudo kut …). {err}
cli.usage:
{app} {version} — {tagline}

Usage:
  kut init   -endpoint <ip|hostname> [-port 51820] [-subnet 10.77.0.0/24] [-iface wg0] [-lang tr|en] [-data DIR] [-dry-run]
  kut passwd [-data DIR] [-user ACCOUNT]
  kut serve  [-data DIR] [-listen ADDR:PORT] [-dry-run]
  kut add    -name NAME [-note NOTE] [-ip IP] [-internet] [-policy PROFILE] [-expires 8h|3d|2w] [-o file.conf]   (adds a device to the running service, prints a QR code)
  kut list   [-data DIR]                                                              (lists devices)
  kut doctor [-data DIR] [-json]                                                      (checks the installation; exit code 1 on errors)
  kut 2fa-off [-data DIR] [-user ACCOUNT]                                                         (turns off panel 2FA; recovery for a lost phone)
  kut backup  [-data DIR] [-o file.tar.gz] [-encrypt]                                (settings + device backup; contains PRIVATE KEYS; -encrypt protects it with a passphrase)
  kut restore -f file.tar.gz [-data DIR] [-force] [-endpoint NEW-IP|HOSTNAME]       (restores while the service is stopped; asks for the passphrase if encrypted)
  kut install [--endpoint X] [--port N] [--subnet CIDR] [--iface NAME] [--device NAME] [--lang tr|en] [--yes]   (installs or upgrades this binary as a service; root)
  kut uninstall [-purge] [-yes] [-dry-run]                                     (removes Kut; writes an encrypted backup first; -purge also deletes the data)
  kut version

-dry-run: does not touch wg/iptables, writes the configuration to the data directory. For trying things out locally.

flag.add_expires: guest device: turns off after this time (e.g. 8h, 3d, 2w)
flag.add_out: also write the configuration to this file (0600)
flag.add_no_qr: do not print a QR code
flag.init_endpoint: the server's public IP or hostname (required)
flag.init_dry_run: do not touch the real wg configuration
flag.init_allow_overlap: continue even if the subnet overlaps a network on this machine
flag.init_lang: server default language: tr or en (notifications, the CLI and kut doctor follow it; if omitted, the environment language, otherwise tr)
flag.serve_listen: address to listen on (default: <VPN server IP>:5000, 127.0.0.1:5000 in dry-run)

init.bad_subnet: -subnet must be a private IPv4 subnet (inside 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 or 100.64/10; between /{min} and /{max}, e.g. 10.77.0.0/24)
init.subnet_not_network: -subnet must start at the network address (e.g. {want})
init.already: {data} is already initialised; the keys are kept, nothing was done
init.conf_exists: {conf} already exists; stopping so as not to overwrite an existing VPN (add -force if you really want to)
init.overlap: -subnet {net} overlaps the {local} network on this machine; pick another network (e.g. {example}) or add -allow-overlap if you mean it

passwd.saved_live: Password saved; the account's open sessions were closed.
passwd.saved_restart: Password saved. Restart the service to close open sessions: sudo systemctl restart kut

add.policy_missing: there is no access profile named "{name}"
add.shown_once: This configuration is shown only now; the private key is not stored on the server.
add.scan: On your phone: WireGuard app > Add tunnel > Scan QR code.

list.empty: No devices yet. To add one: kut add -name ALI

span.too_long: the duration can be at most 1 year

qr.too_long: data is too long for a QR code
